title: Less impressed with longterm use.
text:
** Updated edit. After about 6 months of use, I wish I never paid for Doppler and am returning to Apple Music (UGH!!!)

PROS: Clean UI; there are never ads. You try it, you like it, you buy it. Period. Ability to edit metadata. Reads most types of music files. There’s a Lock Screen widget. Moderate ability to organize music the way you want. 

CONS: The app is not maintained or updated. 

I thought I could use Doppler’s category of “Collections” the same way as Playlist Folders in Apple, but it’s not working out. You can create a Folder (Collection) and put albums inside it, but if you have a Folder of compilations, the songs won’t auto play continuously. You MUST use the built in “Compilations” or “Playlist” option which are on different pages. It’s just not a cohesive system. 

All I want is a music player that I can 100% control how the music files I own are organized. 

Doppler put my Pink Floyd, The Wall album into “Compilations” all on its own. I’ve checked the metadata of every single song (repeatedly) to try and get it out of there with no success. 

There is no option to delete, hide or collapse the built in categories of “Recently Added,” “Compilations,” “Released This Year,” and “Released Last Year.” I’m never using those folders. I DONT WANT TO LOOK AT THEM. 

Importing music is tedious, and there’s NO OPTION TO SYNC ACROSS DEVICES. Metadata is Cap Specific. So songs from the same artist and same album will be automatically put into different albums because a single letter in the artist name or album is different upper/lower case. I had to relabel a LOT of songs because of this. And, guess what! Doppler freezes when editing metadata. I had to shut it down and restart it more times than I bothered to count. 

CONCLUSION: Not worth the $9. The 7 day trial isn’t long enough to discover all of its flaws. And, I wouldn’t have purchased if I’d noticed it hadn’t been updated in over a year. This music player is on the right track, but it really needs some TLC and polishing. Unfortunately, it appears the developers have abandoned it.

title: Disappointed
text:
I was looking for an alternative to Apple’s Music app. This was pretty good, but it lacks many basic features.

The biggest disappointment was the inability to browse or filter my music by genre, which is critical for how I listen.

Also, I wasn’t able to rate songs using a 5-star system. My imported library from macOS has that information. It’s important to me to be able to add or adjust ratings on the go with iOS, and have that synced back to my Mac.

Lastly, Doppler didn’t display any cover art from my synced Mac library. I worked hard over the years manually maintaining that. The cover art is stored in the files themselves, so why not display it?

I’ll be looking for an alternative app now.
